sqlfluff capitalisation and layout findings (CP01/CP02 and others) on usp_run_daily_load are left as they are. The procedure keeps its Phase 1 lower-case style, following the 'write new code in the style of the code around it' rule for changed existing objects.
notes:
Layercake.usp_run_daily_load has one change: after usp_load_gold it calls EXEC Layercake.usp_run_payment_segments @run_id = @run_id. It passes no @as_of_date, so the attributes load uses the run date. The header comment says why the segments run last. Parameters, the run's own logging, the TRY/CATCH (log 'Failed', re-raise the error) and the Phase 1 steps are unchanged, and it still opens no transaction of its own. usp_run_payment_segments is not changed. The down script puts back the Phase 1 definition, and the round-trip passes. Starting point: 4 of the Tester's 13 tests passed and 9 failed. Now all 13, plus 2 developer tests, pass. The developer tests (test_MOD023_dev) check that the segment run is called exactly once, after bronze, silver and gold, with the daily run_id and a NULL as-of date, also under @FullRebuild = 1. They also check that a segment-run error reaches the caller unchanged, that the daily run row ends 'Failed' with the message, and that the Phase 1 steps ran first. For the Technical Writer (MOD-023 documentation update, AC-018-10 / AC-021): the runbook should name usp_run_daily_load as the only procedure to schedule. usp_run_payment_segments, @RebuildFrom and @FullRebuild should be described as optional manual tools, and the one-off rebuild and pending-row steps removed. The header comment in usp_run_payment_segments still says 'A human schedules it after the Phase 1 run'. That object is outside this module's plan, so I left it unchanged; the runbook should take precedence.

Test-first: the first run had 4 of 13 of the Tester's tests passing; the final run passed 13 of 13 and 2 unit test(s), in 4 run(s).
